title: Journey Inventory
description: Schema for the UK commercial bank journey inventory. Each journey represents a discrete end-to-end business scenario (a persona achieving a goal through one or more capabilities). Journeys are the primary unit of work for behavioural modelling, domain-driven design event storming, and test scenario derivation.

recommended_first_journey.description: The single journey that should be modelled first in an event-storming workshop. Chosen because it establishes the foundational domain entities (Customer, Account) that the greatest number of other journeys depend on.

id.description: JRN-XXX reference to a journey in the journeys array.

rationale.description: Explanation of why this journey should be modelled first.

journeys.description: Ordered list of all identified business journeys. Ordering is informational only; use priority and depends_on_journeys for delivery sequencing.

id.description: Stable unique identifier for the journey. Format: JRN-XXX where XXX is a zero-padded integer.

name.description: Short human-readable name for the journey. Used as a label in workshop facilitation and programme planning.

description.description: One to three sentence explanation of the journey scope: who, what, and why. Includes the regulatory or commercial driver where material.

triggering_persona.description: The primary persona who initiates or is the subject of this journey. References a persona ID from the personas artefacts (PER-XXX).

capabilities_touched.description: Top-level capabilities (CAP-XXX) exercised by this journey. At least one required. Order is informational.

sub_capabilities_involved.description: Specific sub-capabilities (CAP-XXX.XX) exercised within the journey. Should be a subset of sub-capabilities belonging to the top-level capabilities listed in capabilities_touched.

cross_capability.description: True if the journey exercises sub-capabilities from two or more distinct top-level capabilities. False if all sub-capabilities belong to a single top-level capability.

priority.description: Delivery priority tier. critical = regulatory prerequisite that must be modelled before the bank can legally operate the relevant service; high = commercially important or regulatory obligation with a defined future deadline; medium = significant business value but not blocking; low = useful but can be deferred without commercial or regulatory consequence.

priority_rationale.description: Explanation of the priority assignment, citing the specific regulatory instrument, service dependency tier, or commercial driver that determined the priority level.

estimated_complexity.description: Indicative complexity of the journey for event-storming workshop planning. simple = single capability, linear happy path, few domain events (<10); moderate = 1-2 capabilities, branching logic, 10-20 domain events; complex = multi-capability, significant branching, regulatory checkpoints, or real-time constraints, >20 domain events.

happy_path_summary.description: A terse numbered-step or prose description of the successful end-to-end flow for this journey, from the triggering event to the successful outcome. Should be sufficient to orient an event-storming facilitator.

depends_on_journeys.description: Other journeys (JRN-XXX) that must be modelled first because they establish domain entities or aggregate roots that this journey extends or references. An empty array means no prerequisite journeys. This is a modelling dependency, not a technical runtime dependency.
